title: Annotatio III §.X (3)(a): Praxis Christiana — first table; latria of what every sense calls bread and wine
pass_a_gloss: (3.) By Christian Praxis, as to the prior Table of the Divine Law, (a) by religiously venerating the whole Triune God: since in the Mass that very thing which all the senses testify to be bread and wine (the species or accidents of these not only exposing their substances to the eyes, but entering as particles into their constitution) is both believed and preached to be the highest God, and is offered and commanded to be adored by communicants, nay by any standing at the Mass celebration, with that very cult proper to the highest God, which the Pontificians themselves discriminate by the name λατρεία from every other inferior cult.
pass_b_english: (3)(a) Christian praxis vs the first table: religious worship of the Triune God.

In the Mass what every sense calls bread and wine (accidents showing and composing the thing) is believed and preached as the highest God, and commanded to communicants and bystanders under latria — the cult Pontificians themselves wall off from every lesser cult.
source_text: (3.) Praxi Christiana, quà priorem Legis Divinæ Tabulam, (a) Naturali de toto Triuno Deo religiosâ veneratione colendo: quandoquidem in Missa illud ipsum, quod sensus omnes testantur panem ac vinum esse (speciebus seu accidentibus horum, non tantùm substantias suas oculis exponentibus, sed, ceu particulas, eorum constitutionem ingredientibus) summus Deus & creditur, & prædicatur esse, & illo ipso cultu, qui summo Deo proprius est, quique à pontificiis ipsis, per λατρείας nomen ab omni alio inferiori cultu discriminatur, Communicaturis, quin Missæ Celebrationi adstantibus quibusvis, adorandum præbetur atque edicitur.

lemmas.latin: sensus omnes testantur panem ac vinum
lemmas.gloss: all the senses testify bread and wine
